title: "Resources: Change control for regulated systems"

Each link below was checked this session and loads.

- **[21 CFR 606.100 — Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.100)**
  — the SOP (standard operating procedure) regulation this module's citations both come from:
  the "establish, maintain, and follow" requirement in paragraph (b), and the sentence requiring
  procedures to be available where they're performed. Local verbatim copy:
  `sources/cfr/606.100.md`.

- **[AABB Quality Systems Framework (2021, public discussion draft PDF)](https://www.aabb.org/docs/default-source/default-document-library/standards/aabb-quality-systems-framework-2021.pdf?sfvrsn=a11081d1_2)**
  — AABB's own public description of the ten Quality System Essentials, including QSE 5,
  Process Control, the home of change control in this module. Use it to see the theme and
  scope of Process Control in AABB's own words; don't cite a standard number from it — see
  `sources/aabb/qse-framework.md` for why.

- **[GovInfo: Code of Federal Regulations collection](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/collection/cfr)**
  — the U.S. Government Publishing Office's official CFR collection. Use it as a fallback
  primary source if eCFR or Cornell is ever unreachable, or to pull an official PDF of a full
  CFR part for the record.

- **[Change Control in Pharmaceuticals | Management Of Change l GMP Change Control
  Explained](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yu9IoENaTk4)** (PharmaZonner- Pharmaceutical
  Knowledge, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson. A
  pharmaceutical-industry educational channel walking the same five-stage request → impact/risk
  assessment → approval → implementation → verification shape this lesson teaches, argued from
  GMP (current good manufacturing practice) drug manufacturing generally rather than blood
  establishments specifically — not AABB-specific, not tied to 606.100(b), and it never mentions
  Lakeshore. Use it to see the same change-control discipline argued from outside the
  blood-specific lens. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Atlassian ITSM: IT Change Management — ITIL Framework & Best
  Practices](https://www.atlassian.com/itsm/change-management)** — a well-regarded ITSM
  vendor's explainer on ITIL 4's change enablement practice (the practice this lesson's "CAB
  under a validated state" bridge is built on), including why ITIL 4 renamed change management
  to change enablement. Use it to see the practice argued in full on its own terms before
  applying the regulated-change overlay this lesson adds on top. Verified loading via `curl` on
  2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Atlassian ITSM: What Is a CAB? Change Advisory Board
  Explained](https://www.atlassian.com/itsm/change-management/change-advisory-board)** — the
  same publisher's dedicated explainer on change advisory boards generally: who sits on one,
  what it reviews, and how it scores risk in an ordinary (non-regulated) change process. Read
  this first, then re-read this lesson's point that a regulated CAB has to score a second axis —
  compliance state, not just service risk — that a generic CAB was never built to catch.
  Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[ICH Q10: Pharmaceutical Quality System (official guideline
  PDF)](https://database.ich.org/sites/default/files/Q10%20Guideline.pdf)** — the International
  Council for Harmonisation's own guideline text, Step 4 version, dated 4 June 2008. ICH Q10 is
  the pharmaceutical-industry quality-system framework (built, like AABB's QSEs, around a
  structured change management system as one of its core elements) that the GMP video above
  draws on — a guidance-tier, cross-industry counterpart to AABB's Process Control QSE, not
  AABB-specific and not binding on Lakeshore directly, but the same underlying "change under a
  quality system" logic. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200; a genuine 21-page
  PDF, confirmed by extracting its text).

- **[FDA: Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/q10-pharmaceutical-quality-system)**
  — FDA's own guidance-document page confirming its adoption of the ICH Q10 guideline above.
  Use this to see how a non-AABB regulatory body (FDA, for drug manufacturers) formally
  recognizes the same change-management-within-a-quality-system concept this lesson applies to
  Lakeshore under AABB's framework instead. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP
  200).

## Keep learning

Not official sources — good places to learn more about change control, including its security-operations side (CISSP Domain 7, Security Operations).

- **[Patching & Change Management MindMap (4 of 6) | CISSP Domain 7](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yTylLQBF6CQ)** (Destination Certification, video) — A CISSP-prep mind-map walk through change requests, impact review and approval. Supports CISSP Domain 7. Supports CISSP Domain 7. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
